_meta.purpose: Structured NPS and government-scheme data for the app's information section and comparison tools.
_meta.next_rate_notification: Due around 30 September 2026 for Q3 FY 2026-27 (Oct-Dec 2026). NOT YET ISSUED as at compile date.
_meta.rate_freeze_context: DEA O.M. dated 30 June 2026 (F.No. 1/4/2019-NS series) kept Q2 rates unchanged from Q1. Small-savings rates have now been static for about nine consecutive quarters; the last real change was Q4 FY 2023-24, effective 1 January 2024.
_meta.CRITICAL_ENGINEERING_NOTE: Small-savings rates are notified QUARTERLY. Every rate in this file must be stored with its effective quarter and refreshed at the end of March, June, September and December. A hard-coded rate will be wrong within 90 days. Build the quarterly refresh before you build the UI.
_meta.full_research_notes: See RESEARCH_nps_and_govt_schemes.md in this folder for scheme-by-scheme sourcing, premature-exit penalties and per-figure citations.

tier_1.nature: Mandatory retirement account, non-withdrawable until exit conditions are met
tier_1.eligibility: Indian citizen (resident, NRI or OCI), age 18-70 at entry
tier_1.dormancy_rule: Below the annual minimum the account is frozen; reactivation costs a Rs 100 penalty plus arrears
tier_1.lock_in: Until normal exit. For the All-Citizen Model this is now 15 years of subscription OR age 60, whichever is earlier

tier_2.eligibility: Requires an active Tier I; same age band
tier_2.confidence: unverified on the minimum initial contribution - sources give both Rs 1,000 and Rs 250

E.name: Equity and related instruments
E.cap_active_choice: 75% (tapering applies above age 50 in Active Choice)

A.name: Alternative investment funds (CMBS/MBS/REITs/InvITs/AIF Cat I and II)

auto_choice_lifecycle_funds.name: Balanced Life Cycle
auto_choice_lifecycle_funds.availability: Private sector only - All-Citizen and Corporate models

tax_treatment._note: Section numbers under the Income-tax Act 2025 are marked where the mapping was not independently confirmed.

own_contribution_employee.limit: 10% of Basic+DA, within the Rs 1,50,000 aggregate ceiling

own_contribution_self_employed.limit: 20% of gross total income, within Rs 1,50,000

additional_deduction.note: Over and above the Rs 1.5 lakh cap

nps_vatsalya.limit: Rs 50,000, SHARED with s.124(3) - not additional

aggregate_employer_cap.excess_treatment: Taxable perquisite, plus tax on the income accruing on the excess

annuity.pension_received: taxable as salary or other income in the year of receipt

tax_treatment.anti_double_deduction: s.124(3)/(4) cannot be claimed on an amount already allowed under s.123. 'Salary' for s.124 means basic pay plus dearness allowance only.

CRITICAL_MISMATCH.issue: PFRDA now permits up to 80% lump sum at normal exit, but the income-tax exemption is still capped at 60% of the corpus. The 20% slice between 60% and 80% is TAXABLE AT SLAB RATES.
CRITICAL_MISMATCH.status: No Budget 2026 amendment raising the exemption to 80% was found.
CRITICAL_MISMATCH.action: RE-VERIFY before showing users a lump-sum figure. This is the kind of gap that produces a nasty surprise for a retiree, and an app that gets it wrong is worse than no app.

exit_rules_non_government.normal_exit_definition: All-Citizen: 15 years of subscription OR age 60, whichever is earlier. Corporate: retirement or superannuation.
exit_rules_non_government.normal_exit_split: Up to 80% lump sum / at least 20% annuity (liberalised from 60/40)
exit_rules_non_government.premature_exit_split: Up to 20% lump sum / at least 80% annuity (unchanged)
exit_rules_non_government.on_death: 100% lump sum to nominee, plus new SLW and SUR phased-payout options; annuity optional

partial_withdrawal.max_amount: 25% of the subscriber's OWN contributions (excludes employer contributions and investment returns)
permitted_reasons: Purchase or construction of a FIRST residential house
Medical treatment or hospitalisation of subscriber, spouse, children or dependent parents (widened from a closed critical-illness list)
Settling a financial obligation to a regulated lender against a lien on the account (new)
partial_withdrawal.lien_facility: Regulated lenders may place a lien or charge on the NPS account up to 25% of own contributions

historical_returns_by_asset_class._caveat: Point-to-point returns as published. Show rolling returns if you can - point-to-point is flattering or damning depending entirely on the end date.

ups.name: Unified Pension Scheme
ups.option_deadline: 30 November 2025 - extended twice (from 30 June and 30 September 2025) and now CLOSED
ups.status: No further extension notified. Employees who did not opt remain in NPS. No belated-application mechanism.
ups.app_note: Present this as historical context, not as an available choice.

apy.name: Atal Pension Yojana
apy.regulator: PFRDA; distributed through banks and post offices
apy.eligibility: Indian citizen aged 18-40 with a savings bank or post office savings account, Aadhaar and mobile linked
apy.income_tax_payer_bar: Anyone who IS or HAS BEEN an income-tax payer cannot join on or after 1 October 2022. IMPORTANT for a tax app - most of your users are disqualified. Present APY as information, not as a recommendation.
apy.contribution_basis: A fixed monthly amount determined by entry age and chosen pension slab, actuarially set. The Government GUARANTEES the pension regardless of fund performance; any shortfall is met by GoI.

indicative_monthly_contribution._warning: Sources disagree at the top end (Rs 1,318 vs Rs 1,454 at age 40 for the Rs 5,000 slab). Use the official Jansuraksha chart, not either secondary source.

apy.corpus_to_nominee: About Rs 1.7 lakh for the Rs 1,000 slab, rising to about Rs 8.5 lakh for the Rs 5,000 slab
apy.on_death: Spouse receives the same pension for life; on the spouse's death, the corpus goes to the nominee
apy.exit_before_60: Permitted. Own contributions plus net accrued returns are refunded; government co-contribution and its returns are forfeited.
apy.govt_co_contribution: Only for those who joined between 1 June 2015 and 31 March 2016, for 5 years. NOT available to new joiners.

tax.contribution: 80CCD(1) within Rs 1.5L plus 80CCD(1B) up to Rs 50,000, i.e. s.123 / s.124(3). OLD REGIME ONLY.
tax.pension_received: Taxable at slab rates (not explicitly confirmed in sources)

post_office_savings_account.compounding: calculated on balance between the 10th and month end, credited annually

time_deposit_3yr.note: A TaxGuru table showing 7.00% is WRONG - cross-checked against Indian Bank and India Post reproductions

time_deposit_5yr.tax_benefit: 80C / s.123 - the ONLY time deposit that qualifies

mssc.status: CLOSED to new accounts - locked rate for existing holders only

schemes.name: Public Provident Fund
schemes.interest_calc_quirk: Interest accrues on the MINIMUM balance between the 5th and the last day of each month. Deposit by the 5th or lose a month's interest - a genuinely useful tip for the app to surface.
schemes.tenure: 15 financial years, extendable indefinitely in 5-year blocks with or without further contributions
schemes.max_basis: per financial year, aggregate across all PPF accounts including a minor's
schemes.eligibility: Resident individual; one account per person; a guardian may open for a minor. NRIs cannot open new accounts - an existing account runs to maturity with no extension.
schemes.loan: Years 3-6; up to 25% of the balance at the end of the second preceding year; interest 1% above the PPF rate; repay in 36 months
schemes.partial_withdrawal: From year 7; once per financial year; lower of 50% of the balance 4 years prior and 50% of the prior-year balance
schemes.premature_closure: After 5 years only for a life-threatening illness (self, spouse, children, dependent parents), higher education, or change of residency status. Penalty: interest recomputed 1% lower for the whole period.
schemes.tax: EEE. Contribution 80C / s.123; interest and maturity exempt.
schemes.where: Post office; SBI and nationalised banks; ICICI, HDFC, Axis and other authorised private banks; online in most

schemes.name: Employees' Provident Fund
schemes.rate_fy2026_27: NOT YET DECLARED. Historically announced in Feb-Mar of the FOLLOWING year, so around Feb-Mar 2027. DO NOT DISPLAY a FY 2026-27 EPF rate.
schemes.rate_authority: Recommended by the CBT at its 239th meeting on 2 March 2026, ratified by Government (PIB PRID 2234502)
schemes.compounding: Calculated monthly on the running balance, credited annually
schemes.contribution: Employee 12% of wages; employer 12% (8.33% to EPS capped at Rs 15,000 wage, 3.67% to EPF) plus 0.50% EDLI and admin charges
schemes.new_scheme: EPF Scheme 2026 notified 29 June 2026 under the Code on Social Security 2020, replacing the 1952 Scheme. EPS 2026 and EDLI 2026 also notified. The Rs 15,000 ceiling was retained.
schemes.tax_contribution: Employee's share: 80C / s.123, old regime only. Employer's share exempt within the Rs 7.5 lakh aggregate cap.
schemes.tax_interest: Interest on EMPLOYEE contributions above Rs 2,50,000 a year is TAXABLE (from FY 2021-22). The threshold is Rs 5,00,000 where there is no employer contribution, such as GPF. EPFO maintains separate taxable and non-taxable accounts.
schemes.tax_withdrawal: Exempt after 5 years of continuous service; otherwise taxable with TDS

schemes.name: Voluntary Provident Fund
schemes.limit: Up to 100% of wages, subject to the new cap of wages net of permitted deductions under s.18(2) of the Code on Wages 2019
schemes.employer_match: Optional, not obligatory under EPF Scheme 2026
schemes.exit: Under EPF Scheme 2026 either party may unilaterally reduce or discontinue voluntary contributions - previously a joint option was required
schemes.tax: Same as EPF. VPF counts toward the Rs 2.5 lakh taxable-interest threshold - the most commonly missed point about VPF.

schemes.name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
schemes.eligibility: Resident girl child under 10 at opening; one account per girl, maximum two per family (more for twins or triplets with a certificate)
schemes.maturity: 21 years from opening, or on marriage after 18
schemes.partial_withdrawal: After the girl turns 18 or passes 10th standard - up to 50% of the prior-year balance, for higher education
schemes.premature_closure: After 5 years on specified grounds (death, life-threatening illness, death of guardian); after 18 for marriage
schemes.tax: EEE. 80C / s.123; interest and maturity exempt.
schemes.where: Post offices and authorised banks; in-person KYC required

schemes.name: Senior Citizens Savings Scheme
schemes.eligibility: Age 60+; 55-60 for civilian retirees within one month of receiving retirement benefits; 50-60 for retired defence personnel. Joint account only with a spouse. NRIs and HUFs excluded.
schemes.tenure: 5 years, extendable by 3 years (apply within one year of maturity)
schemes.max_basis: per individual across all SCSS accounts, in multiples of Rs 1,000
schemes.premature_closure: Before 1 year: no interest, and interest already paid is recovered. 1-2 years: 1.5% of deposit deducted. After 2 years: 1% deducted.
schemes.tax: Deposit qualifies for 80C / s.123 (old regime). Interest is FULLY TAXABLE; senior-citizen interest deduction under 80TTB / s.153.
schemes.tds_threshold: Rs 1,00,000 a year under s.194A for senior citizens, from FY 2025-26
schemes.where: Post offices; SBI, HDFC, ICICI, Axis and other authorised banks
schemes.app_note: The headline 8.20% is fully taxable. For a 30%-bracket investor the post-tax return is about 5.54%, below tax-free PPF at 7.10%. Show the post-tax comparison.

schemes.name: National Savings Certificate (VIII Issue)
schemes.rate_lock: Locks at purchase for the full term
schemes.eligibility: Resident individual, including on behalf of a minor; joint accounts allowed. NRIs and HUFs excluded.
schemes.premature: Not allowed, except on death of the holder, a court order, or forfeiture by a pledgee
schemes.loan: Can be pledged as security with banks
schemes.tax: Deposit qualifies for 80C / s.123. Accrued interest of years 1-4 is deemed reinvested and ALSO qualifies for 80C - a genuinely underused feature. Year-5 interest is taxable. No TDS.

schemes.name: Kisan Vikas Patra
schemes.maturity_note: Money doubles in 9 years 7 months at the current rate. Rate locks at purchase.
schemes.premature: After 2 years 6 months; earlier only on death, court order or pledge forfeiture
schemes.tax: NO 80C deduction. Interest fully taxable, on either an accrual or a receipt basis.

schemes.name: Post Office Monthly Income Scheme
schemes.eligibility: Resident individual 18+; a minor via guardian, with the minor's own limit of Rs 3 lakh (unverified)
schemes.premature: Not before 1 year. 1-3 years: 2% of deposit deducted. 3-5 years: 1% deducted.
schemes.tax: No 80C. Interest fully taxable. No TDS on MIS itself, but aggregate post office interest counts for s.194A.

schemes.name: Post Office Time Deposits
schemes.premature: Not before 6 months. Closed at 6-12 months: PO Savings Account rate (4%). 2/3/5-year TDs closed after 1 year: 2% below the applicable TD rate.
schemes.tax: ONLY the 5-year TD qualifies for 80C / s.123. Interest taxable in all cases.

schemes.name: Post Office Recurring Deposit (5-year)
schemes.min_basis: per month, in multiples of Rs 10
schemes.loan: Up to 50% of the balance after 12 monthly deposits
schemes.premature: After 3 years; interest then paid at the PO Savings Account rate
schemes.default_penalty: Rs 1 per Rs 100 per month rebate/penalty structure

schemes.name: Post Office Savings Account
schemes.compounding: calculated on the balance between the 10th and month end, credited annually
schemes.tax: Interest exempt up to Rs 3,500 single / Rs 7,000 joint under 10(15)(i) (not re-verified). Beyond that, 80TTA (Rs 10,000) or 80TTB (Rs 50,000 for seniors) / s.153, old regime only.
schemes.where: Post offices; cheque book, ATM and mobile/net banking available

schemes.name: RBI Floating Rate Savings Bonds, 2020 (Taxable)
schemes.rate_basis: NSC rate (7.70%) plus a 0.35% spread, reset every 6 months
schemes.interest_payment: Half-yearly on 1 January and 1 July. NO cumulative option.
schemes.eligibility: Resident individuals and HUFs. NRIs not eligible.
schemes.premature_exit: Senior citizens only: 60-70 after 6 years; 70-80 after 5 years; 80+ after 4 years - with a penalty of 50% of the last half-year's interest
schemes.tax: Interest fully taxable at slab rates. No 80C.
schemes.app_note: The highest-yielding fully sovereign instrument currently available at 8.05%, but it is fully taxable and has no cumulative option, so it suits someone who needs income rather than accumulation.

closed_to_new_money.name: Mahila Samman Savings Certificate (MSSC)
closed_to_new_money.status: CLOSED to new accounts from 31 March 2025
closed_to_new_money.detail: A two-year scheme launched April 2023. Existing holders keep 7.5% compounded quarterly to maturity; the last accounts mature by 31 March 2027. Maximum Rs 2 lakh per woman. Partial withdrawal of 40% after 1 year (one source says 6 months - unverified). Premature closure allowed after 6 months at 2% lower. Interest fully taxable, no 80C.

closed_to_new_money.name: Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY)
closed_to_new_money.status: CLOSED to new subscriptions from 31 March 2023
closed_to_new_money.detail: LIC-operated. Existing policyholders keep their locked rate (7.4% for the final cohort) for the full 10-year term, payable monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annually. Not extended. The practical successor for seniors is SCSS.

closed_to_new_money.name: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB)
closed_to_new_money.detail: Last tranche February 2024 (2023-24 Series IV). No issuance calendar for FY 2025-26 or FY 2026-27. The Government cited it as a high-cost borrowing method.

tax_on_redemption.original_subscriber_premature_with_rbi_a: Exempt - CONTESTED. Some commentary says only redemptions before 1 April 2026 qualify.
tax_on_redemption.budget_2026_change: Reported to restrict the exemption to original subscribers holding to maturity. Single-sourced. VERIFY.
